data.name: Bujair
data.gender_notes: Bujair is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'Baqara' meaning 'cow', this name was given to the Prophet Muhammad's (pbuh) companion, Bujair ibn Hudaifah. It is said that Bujair's light shone like a beacon during the Battle of Badr, illuminating the darkness and guiding his companions to victory. The name Bujair carries the meaning “Bright, Radiant” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Bujair usually hope their child will grow to embody bright, radiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A shining beacon of faith and courage.
data.etymology: Bujair belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Bright, Radiant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bujair total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: Bujair is named after the Prophet Muhammad's (pbuh) companion, who hailed from the Ribbah tribe. In Islamic history, Bujair is remembered for his courage and bravery during the Battle of Badr, which took place in 624 AD. According to historical records, Bujair's tribe initially refused to join the Muslim army, but when the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) invited the women and children to emigrate to Medina, they changed their minds and joined the Muslim forces. Bujair played a pivotal role in the Battle of Badr, leading a group of fighters and providing crucial support to the Muslim army. After the battle, Bujair's bravery and self-sacrifice became a source of inspiration for other Muslims.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Bujair holds spiritual significance because of the virtue and honor exhibited by its namesake. Bujair's commitment to the Prophet Muhammad's (pbuh) message and his unwavering bravery during the Battle of Badr reflect the spiritual values of loyalty, courage, and self-sacrifice. Muslims believe that every name carries a spiritual meaning and holds a certain energy. By bearing the name Bujair, a person aligns themselves with the spiritual qualities of this noble companion and seeks to embody his virtues in their own life. The name Bujair is, therefore, a reminder of the many virtues and qualities that are valued in Islam, such as courage, self-sacrifice, and devotion to faith.
